rules.statement: When a helper must be duplicated across packages that cannot reference each other, give every copy the same contract (same inputs rejected, same null/failure results) and add a comment, or a convention note, saying why the copy is deliberate and that a change to one copy must be made to all.
rules.why: Undocumented copies drift: the two form-reading helpers already behaved differently on a non-form content type, and a future fix would land in only one place.
rules.check: Look for a new helper whose body repeats an existing helper in another package; compare their edge-case behaviour and check for a comment explaining the duplication.

rules.statement: In production code, an options-validation failure message names the configuration key and quotes the rejected value, but withholds a value that may carry a secret (for example a URI containing user info `@`).
rules.why: An operator whose host won't start can't tell which constraint failed without seeing the value, but credentials must not leak into logs.
rules.check: Look at new or changed IValidateOptions failure messages: does each one include the offending value after the key, and does it suppress values that could contain passwords or other secrets?

rules.statement: In a test project, a test that covers behaviour the change under test does not touch says in its doc comment that it pins existing behaviour, and asserts only what that path actually produces.
rules.why: Otherwise a reader takes the test as evidence for the new code even though it passes without that code.
rules.check: Look for tests added with a change that exercise an endpoint or path the change doesn't modify; check that their doc comment says they pin existing behaviour.

rules.statement: Build absolute redirect URIs and callback URLs from the configured public origin, never from the incoming request's Host header.
rules.why: A forged Host header would otherwise steer the redirect_uri to an attacker-controlled origin.
rules.check: Look for redirect_uri or callback URL construction that uses HttpRequest.Host, Scheme or similar request-derived values rather than a configured origin.

rules.statement: In a test project, a security protection that has unit tests (such as rejecting a forged Host) also gets at least one integration test through the fully assembled host.
rules.why: Unit tests of the handler don't catch a wiring regression in the composed host.
rules.check: When a change adds a security check covered only by unit tests, look for an integration test that drives the real host with the attack input and asserts the protected outcome.
